stem: An engineer runs `terraform plan -out=tfplan` in an environment where multiple developers make changes. Why would they choose to pass `tfplan` to `terraform apply tfplan` instead of running `terraform apply` directly?
options: Passing the pre-generated plan file guarantees that Terraform executes the exact pre-approved changes even if configuration or remote infrastructure changed after the plan was created.
A saved plan file is the only way Terraform can record resource IDs in the state file during an apply operation.
Passing the saved plan file bypasses provider API evaluation during execution so that resources can be provisioned when offline.
The plan command directly provisions resources in dry-run mode, and passing the file to apply commits the transaction to the provider.
objective: Generate, save, and review speculative execution plans using terraform plan

stem: A developer runs `terraform apply` without passing a saved plan file. Terraform displays the planned execution actions and waits for interactive confirmation. The developer types `Y` and presses Enter. What happens next?
options: Terraform aborts execution without modifying any infrastructure because only the exact word 'yes' is accepted to confirm execution.
Terraform defaults to generating a saved plan file on disk instead of applying the changes.
Terraform accepts 'Y' as standard affirmative confirmation and begins provisioning the planned resources.
Terraform applies non-destructive changes but leaves resources requiring recreation unapplied.
objective: Apply changes and destroy infrastructure resources safely against LocalStack to create state snapshots

stem: An engineer finishes testing a staging environment and runs `terraform destroy`. How does Terraform determine which real-world infrastructure objects to remove, and how does this command differ from editing files?
options: Terraform requires every resource block to be manually commented out in configuration files before destroy can execute.
Terraform purges the local state file first, causing the remote cloud provider to detect orphan objects and tear them down.
Terraform scans the cloud provider for any resource matching tags in configuration and deletes them immediately without user confirmation.
Terraform uses state data to identify managed objects and removes them without requiring the developer to delete resource definitions from configuration files.
objective: Apply changes and destroy infrastructure resources safely against LocalStack to create state snapshots
